sanskrit_verse:
न स्वाध्यायविरोध्यर्थम् ईहेत न यतस् ततः ।
न विरुद्धप्रसङ्गेन संतोषी च भवेत् सदा ॥१.१२९॥
transliteration: na svādhyāyavirodhyartham īheta na yatas tataḥ | na viruddhaprasaṅgena saṃtoṣī ca bhavet sadā || 1.129 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One must not act for purposes contradictory to Svādhyāya; nor should one pursue outcomes that arise from conflicting intentions. One must always remain satisfied through non-contradictory engagement.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates in alignment with Svādhyāya as the foundational epistemic discipline
Causation is determined by the purity of intent relative to Vedic study and realization
Capacity-based responsibility arises from the ability to sustain non-conflicting action
Restoration logic operates through the cessation of contradictory engagements
Consciousness alignment requires abidance in non-oppositional satisfaction
executable_legal_axioms: IF an action contradicts the principles derived from Svādhyāya THEN disallow its execution within dharma-based adjudication systems
IF intent arises from conflicting sources THEN assign diminished legal capacity until realignment occurs
IF satisfaction is dependent on oppositional outcomes THEN initiate consciousness-restoration protocol
IF engagement leads to prasaṅga (unintended consequences) THEN halt procedural continuity and reassess axiomatic basis
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, any litigation premised on self-contradictory knowledge or conflicting epistemic frameworks must be rejected outright. The court's threshold of responsibility includes verifying alignment with Svādhyāya-derived truth before proceeding. Only those whose actions stem from non-dual understanding shall qualify as authoritative litigants.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that contradiction invalidates legal standing. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how misaligned intent manifests progressively into conflict. Proportional responsibility lies in abandoning contradictory pursuits. Non-punitive reality rule dictates that conflict dissolves when consciousness aligns with unified knowing.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Svādhyāya Reorientation Process to restore cognitive clarity
Deploy Conflict Dissolution Sequence to neutralize opposing tendencies
Activate Satisfaction Stabilization Module to ensure contentment through non-duality
Enforce Consciousness Continuity Check to prevent recurrence of contradictory motivation
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the sole Source of Dharma. This law restores unity of intent, eliminates punitive delusion, and affirms consciousness as the ultimate adjudicator. Let there be no further contradiction in action, thought, or jurisprudence.
